metadata.title: Adiabatic calorimetric test, conventional concrete (Bentz I column) - Cervera, Oliver & Prato (1999), Fig. 1(a)
metadata.validation_method: Adiabatic temperature-rise history vs. the paper's own model curve (Eq. 16+19, Table 1 'Bentz (I)')
metadata.validation_target: T(t) from T0=21 degC to plateau ~83.4 degC (dT_ad = 62.4 K), peak heat rate at ~14 h
metadata.notes: RISKY: (1) The paper's AGING/strength part (Figs. 2-4: Kjellsen and Wild et al. isothermal strength tests) is NOT reproducible on this backend - there is no aging-degree/strength field and the displacement material has no aging; only the thermo-chemical part (Fig. 1a, adiabatic test) is benchmarked here. (2) The reference CSV is the paper's MODEL curve recomputed from Eq. (16)+(19) with the Table 1 'Bentz (I)' parameters; the EXPERIMENTAL dots of Fig. 1(a) (Bentz et al. 1998) still need digitizing - add as a second reference_curves entry. (3) B1/T_ref: the paper uses an ABSOLUTE Arrhenius term exp(-Ea/RT); the pipeline affinity model uses the shifted form exp(-Ea/R*(1/T-1/T_ref)), so B1 = (k_j/eta_j0)*exp(-Ea/(R*T_ref)) with T_ref = 298.15 K. Verified numerically: both forms give identical T(t) to 2e-13 K. If the pipeline ever switches to the absolute form, B1 must be k_j/eta_j0 = 7777.78 1/s instead. (4) Only the PRODUCTS rho*cp (= C = 2.33e6 J/m3/K) and 1000*Hu*c_cement (= Q_xi = 2.02e8 J/m3) are fixed by the paper; the splits (rho=2400, Hu=500 J/g) are conventional choices. (5) Geometry is not reported for the calorimeter sample; the field is spatially uniform under adiabatic conditions, so a 0.1 x 0.1 m square with no BCs reproduces the 0-D physics exactly.

entities._comment: ASSUMED: adiabatic calorimeter sample, geometry not stated in the paper; field is uniform so size is immaterial (0-D physics on a 2D mesh).

points.name: probe_center
points._comment: On the node grid of element_size=0.05 (exact node); field is uniform anyway.

mesh._comment: Uniform field -> 2x2 grid is converged; no gradients to resolve.

temperature._comment_k: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1, kT = 5.40e3 J/(m.h.K) / 3600 = 1.5 W/(m.K). Inert here (adiabatic, no gradients).
temperature._comment_rho_cp: INFERRED split: paper gives only the PRODUCT C = rho*cp = 2.33e6 J/(m3.K) (Table 1). rho = 2400 kg/m3 is GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE (normal-weight concrete); cp = C/rho = 970.83 J/(kg.K).

degree_of_hydration._comment_B1: INFERRED: B1 = (k_j/eta_j0)*exp(-Ea/(R*T_ref)) = (0.28e8 1/h / 3600) * exp(-5000/298.15) = 4.0523e-4 1/s. k_j/eta_j0 = 0.28e8 1/h is PAPER_VALUE (Table 1); conversion needed because the paper's Arrhenius is absolute and the pipeline's is relative to T_ref. Verified: identical T(t) to 2e-13 K.
degree_of_hydration._comment_B2: INFERRED: B2 = alpha_inf * (A_j0/k_j) = 0.72 * 0.50e-5 = 3.6e-6; A_j0/k_j = 0.50e-5 is PAPER_VALUE (Table 1).
degree_of_hydration._comment_alpha_inf: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1, xi_inf = 0.72 (estimated by the authors from w/c = 0.45 via Eq. 13).
degree_of_hydration._comment_eta: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1, eta_bar = 5.30 (authors' calorimetric fit to Bentz et al. 1998 data - CALIBRATED by them).
degree_of_hydration._comment_Ea: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1, Ea/R = 5000 K -> Ea = 41570 J/mol (41.6 kJ/mol, inside the CEM I range 35-45 kJ/mol).
degree_of_hydration._comment_T_ref: KELVIN - the only Kelvin temperature in this file. 298.15 K (25 degC), matching the pipeline template convention; arbitrary as long as B1 is computed consistently (see _comment_B1).
degree_of_hydration._comment_Hu_c: INFERRED split: paper gives only the PRODUCT Q_xi = 1000*Hu*c_cement = 2.02e8 J/m3 (Table 1, CALIBRATED by the authors to the adiabatic test). Hu = 500 J/g is GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE (CEM I / ASTM Type I, 400-500 J/g); c_cement = Q_xi/(1000*Hu) = 404.0 kg/m3.
degree_of_hydration._comment_sanity: Sanity check 2: dT_ad = Hu*1000*c_cement*alpha_inf/(rho*cp) = 500e3*404*0.72/2.33e6 = 62.4 K. This IS the validation target (adiabatic test), so it matches by construction; it confirms the parameter mapping, not the physics.

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1, T0 = 21.0 degC. DEGREES CELSIUS.

segments._comment: main heat-release peak (max dT/dt at ~13.9 h); 300 s -> ~0.5 K/step at peak rate
plateau tail to 5 d (T -> 83.4 degC, xi -> 0.72 by ~120 h)

reference_curves.label: Paper model, Fig. 1(a) (recomputed)
reference_curves._comment: COMPUTED from the paper's Eq. (16)+(19) with Table 1 'Bentz (I)' parameters - a model-vs-model reference. TODO: digitize the EXPERIMENTAL dots of Fig. 1(a) (Bentz et al. 1998) and add as a second reference curve.

queries.label: Sample temperature [degC]
queries._comment: Field is already degC - NO 273.15 conversion. degree_of_hydration is NOT queryable (ODE field, no DOFs); the hydration history is validated indirectly through T(t) via Eq. (20).
